dedupe_keys.name: shelby county memphis tennessee interdependent buildings water and power testbed in in core mmsa seismic notebooks

description: The Memphis Metropolitan Statistical Area (MMSA) testbed in the IN-CORE documentation models seismic damage and recovery of buildings, potable water infrastructure and electric power infrastructure serving Shelby County, Tennessee, a county of about one million people exposed to earthquakes from the New Madrid Seismic Zone. The scenario is a magnitude 7.9 earthquake with its epicentre north-west of the county. Coverage: Shelby County. The testbed holds physical and demographic data for every building, with structure type, occupancy and number of stories for fragility functions, and the locations of water and power facilities and water pipelines of Memphis Light, Gas and Water, taken from the MAEViz software of the Mid-America Earthquake Center; water comes from the Memphis Aquifer and power from the Tennessee Valley Authority. Two notebooks use pyIncore to compute damages with fragility and repair rate curves, network connectivity based functionality, and restoration with restoration curves; they load ten IN-CORE datasets. Format and access: Jupyter notebooks in the incore-docs repository, with the datasets in the IN-CORE data service, which needs an account. Licence (read on 2026-09-29): MPL-2.0 (pyincore); no LICENSE file in the incore-docs repository holding the testbed notebooks. Caveats: the infrastructure data are older MAEViz layers, not current utility records. Simulation uses: a ready interdependent testbed for cascading failure, resilience and recovery studies. Related records: IN-CORE (platform-in-core) is the platform that runs it.
